story: Alaska DNR's October 13th preliminary finding favors ENSTAR over Hilcorp for a gas storage lease in the depleted Kenai Loop field under the Kenai airport, while the City of Kenai disputes who owns the pore space

claims.claim: The Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas preliminarily found that leasing the Kenai Loop gas storage formation to ENSTAR would best serve the state's interest.
claims.verbatim: for the purposes of gas storage to ENSTAR would best serve the state's interest
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 1 of 20, Introduction. Verified against the showrunner's pypdf extraction (out/2026-10-19/scouts/kenai_loop_prelim.txt). Typographic apostrophe normalized to straight. The extraction is TRUNCATED mid-word on page 17 ('publicly availa'), so claims from pages 17 to 20 were verified separately against rendered page images of the same PDF, fetched 2026-10-20. Corroborated by Alaska Public Media/KDLL October 16th. It is PRELIMINARY. Write 'favors' or 'preliminarily chose', never 'awarded'.

claims.claim: The preliminary written finding is dated October 13th.
claims.verbatim: October 13, 2026 KENAI LOOP GAS FIELD NATURAL GAS STORAGE LEASE Preliminary Written Finding of the Director
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Cover page, pypdf extraction, line breaks joined with spaces. Corroborated by public notice 225521, whose publish date reads 10/13/2026.

claims.claim: ENSTAR filed its Kenai Loop gas storage lease application on May 7th.
claims.verbatim: ENSTAR's on May 7, 2026, and Hilcorp's on May 11, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 2, section II.C. pypdf extraction, apostrophes normalized. This is background inside the window. The applications are older, but they are dated by the October 13th finding.

claims.claim: Hilcorp filed its competing application for the same storage lease on May 11th.
claims.verbatim: ENSTAR's on May 7, 2026, and Hilcorp's on May 11, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 2, section II.C. pypdf extraction. The applicant is Hilcorp Cook Inlet, LLC (page 1).

claims.claim: Both applications sought to use the same reservoir for natural gas storage.
claims.verbatim: These applications both seek authorization to use the same reservoir
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 2, section II.C. pypdf extraction.

claims.claim: DNR said only one operator can feasibly develop and manage storage in a single subsurface reservoir.
claims.verbatim: only one operator can feasibly develop and manage storage in a single subsurface reservoir without causing unreasonable interference
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 2, section II.C. pypdf extraction. DNR stresses that this was not a competitive bidding or ranking exercise (page 3). Do not call it an auction.

claims.claim: The storage formation lies in the Upper Tyonek Formation between 8,600 and 10,500 feet true vertical depth subsea.
claims.verbatim: two distinct intervals in the Upper Tyonek Formation between 8,600 feet and 10,500 feet true vertical depth subsea
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 1, footnote 1, pypdf extraction with the line break joined. The same text is repeated on the Attachment 1 map legend (rendered page image). The source abbreviates it 'TDVSS', apparently a typo for TVDSS.

claims.claim: The shallower 9,700-foot sand averages 44 feet of net reservoir thickness.
claims.verbatim: Net reservoir thicknesses of each sand average 44 feet for the 9,700-foot sand and 65 feet for the 10,000-foot sand
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Footnote 1 (continued on page 2) and the Attachment 1 legend. pypdf splits '10,000-' across a line, and the rendered map legend shows it unbroken.

claims.claim: The deeper 10,000-foot sand averages 65 feet of net reservoir thickness.
claims.verbatim: Net reservoir thicknesses of each sand average 44 feet for the 9,700-foot sand and 65 feet for the 10,000-foot sand
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Same passage as C08.

claims.claim: Coal layers averaging 20 to 30 feet thick provide the seals that contain gas in the formation.
claims.verbatim: Coals, averaging 20-30 feet thick, interbed with silty sands and shales above the top and below the base of each of the two sand intervals, provide the required seals for gas containment
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Footnote 1, page 2. The source prints an en dash between 20 and 30, and it is normalized to a hyphen here under the house no-dash rule. Write '20 to 30 feet' in prose.

claims.claim: ENSTAR's proposed project area contains about 500 acres of state-owned mineral estate.
claims.verbatim: The estimated state-owned mineral estate is approximately 500.00 acres.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 5, section III.B. Corroborated by notice 225521, which says 'approximately 500 acres of State of Alaska owned subsurface gas storage reservoir'. The existing field itself holds only about 147.50 state acres (page 5). The project area also includes Mental Health Trust and CIRI mineral estate.

claims.claim: Hilcorp's larger proposed project area contains about 1,330 acres of state-owned mineral estate.
claims.verbatim: The estimated state-owned mineral estate is approximately 1,330.00 acres.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 6, section III.C. Hilcorp's area spans T5N sections 3 to 6 and T6N sections 19 to 22 and 27 to 34, and it includes City of Kenai and private mineral estate.

claims.claim: ENSTAR estimated about 3.9 billion cubic feet of native gas remains in the Kenai Loop reservoir.
claims.verbatim: This remaining native gas is estimated at about 3.9 billion cubic feet (Bcf) based on ENSTAR's analysis and 6.4 Bcf based on Hilcorp's analysis
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 8, section V. pypdf extraction. Page 14 gives the figure as 3.90 Bcf, based on a 'data-rich P/z plot'. The final terms (page 18, rendered image) adopt 3.9 Bcf. Alaska Public Media rounds it to 'about 4 billion cubic feet'.

claims.claim: Hilcorp estimated about 6.4 billion cubic feet of native gas remains in the reservoir.
claims.verbatim: Hilcorp estimated that 6.4 Bcf of native gas remains in the reservoir, significantly higher than ENSTAR's estimate of 3.9 Bcf
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 15, section IX.A.2, estimate given at the September 3rd technical meeting. Checked against both the pypdf extraction and the rendered page image.

claims.claim: DNR said Hilcorp's higher estimate relied on fewer pressure data points.
claims.verbatim: Hilcorp's interpretation relied on fewer P/z data points, which contributed to its higher estimate.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 15. P/z is reservoir pressure divided by the gas compressibility factor, a standard depletion-plot method.

claims.claim: The Director concluded ENSTAR's remaining gas estimate is the more reliable one.
claims.verbatim: the Director concludes that ENSTAR's estimate is the more reliable representation of remaining native gas
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 15. This is the regulator's conclusion and should be attributed to DNR, not stated as settled fact.

claims.claim: DNR said Hilcorp provided about one quarter of the requested data and information.
claims.verbatim: Hilcorp provided about one quarter of the requested data and information
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.suggested_phrasing: According to DNR, Hilcorp provided about one quarter of the data it requested.
claims.notes: Page 16, section IX.B.2, checked on the pypdf extraction and the rendered image. This is DNR's one-sided characterization. Hilcorp was unable to comment before Alaska Public Media's October 16th story, so attribute it to DNR.

claims.claim: At a September 3rd technical meeting, Hilcorp told DNR it did not have a solid understanding of the reservoir geometry.
claims.verbatim: During the technical meeting Hilcorp shared that they did not have a solid understanding of the reservoir geometry
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.suggested_phrasing: DNR's finding says Hilcorp acknowledged it lacked a solid understanding of the reservoir geometry.
claims.notes: Page 15. Preceded by 'Hilcorp met with the DO&G for a technical meeting on September 3, 2026.' This is DNR's paraphrase of what Hilcorp said, not a Hilcorp quote. Never put it in Hilcorp's mouth in quotation marks.

claims.claim: ENSTAR provided results of a dynamic reservoir model showing injection and production rates.
claims.verbatim: ENSTAR provided results of a dynamic reservoir model showing injectability and production rates supporting the delivery of stored gas to Railbelt customers
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 16, section IX.B.1. A physics-based simulation model, not AI. Do not frame it as AI.

claims.claim: DNR said Hilcorp did not present a dynamic model.
claims.verbatim: did not present a dynamic model
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 16, the same sentence as C17.

claims.claim: Fully built out with nine wells, ENSTAR plans peak withdrawal and injection capacity of 150 million standard cubic feet per day.
claims.verbatim: Under a fully developed nine well scenario, ENSTAR plans to have peak withdrawal and injection capacity of 150 million standard cubic feet per day (MMscf/D).
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.suggested_phrasing: ENSTAR plans up to 150 million standard cubic feet per day once nine wells are in service.
claims.notes: Page 16. This is a plan, not built capacity. Nine wells means three existing plus up to six Phase 2 wells (C26).

claims.claim: In the initial three-well phase, ENSTAR's rates would be roughly 30 percent of full capacity.
claims.verbatim: During the initial three-well scenario, those rates would be scaled down to roughly 30%.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 16. Arithmetic check: 30 percent of 150 is about 45 MMscf/D. That figure is DERIVED and not printed, so if the deck uses it, label it as approximate.

claims.claim: ENSTAR's total working gas volume would be about 20.5 billion cubic feet.
claims.verbatim: In either case, the total working gas volume would be about 20.5 Bcf and the cushion gas volumes would be approximately 8 Bcf.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 16. Sanity check: 20.5 working plus 8 cushion is 28.5 Bcf, below the 32.5 Bcf original gas in place (C49), which is consistent. ADN's July 10th '25 billion cubic feet initially' (C69) is a different metric reported earlier. This is the authoritative working-gas figure for the deck.

claims.claim: ENSTAR's plan would keep about 8 billion cubic feet of cushion gas in the reservoir.
claims.verbatim: the cushion gas volumes would be approximately 8 Bcf
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 16. Cushion gas is the gas left in place to maintain pressure.

claims.claim: ENSTAR proposes operating the field up to its discovery pressure of 5,395 pounds per square inch.
claims.verbatim: ENSTAR proposes operating the field up to the discovery pressure of 5,395 pounds per square inch (psi).
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 16, section IX.C.1.

claims.claim: ENSTAR's initial plan reuses three existing wells, with up to six more possible in a later phase.
claims.verbatim: The initial plan would re-use three of the existing wells for storage operations
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 16. Also on the page is 'A future Phase 2 could see up to six additional wells being drilled'. 3 plus 6 equals 9, which matches C21.

claims.claim: Hilcorp proposed drilling four new wells for its storage facility.
claims.verbatim: The initial proposal includes plans to drill four new, grassroots wells
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 17, section IX.C.2. Verified on the rendered page image only, because the pypdf extraction ends before this passage. Hilcorp's plan also included a new pad of about 3.75 acres and a new pipeline.

claims.claim: Hilcorp's initial application put its working gas volume at about 28 to 33 billion cubic feet.
claims.verbatim: Hilcorp stated that under a four well scenario, a working gas volume would be about 28 to 33 Bcf
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.suggested_phrasing: Hilcorp's initial application claimed 28 to 33 Bcf of working gas, a figure it later revised sharply downward, according to DNR.
claims.notes: Page 17, rendered image. Use it ONLY together with C32: at the September 3rd meeting Hilcorp presented 'significantly reduced' working volumes, and the application was never amended. Do not compare it head to head with ENSTAR's 20.5 Bcf as though both stand.

claims.claim: Hilcorp's application listed a maximum withdrawal rate of 20 to 30 million standard cubic feet per day.
claims.verbatim: with a maximum withdrawal rate of 20 to 30 MMscf/D
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 17, rendered image.

claims.claim: Hilcorp's application listed a maximum operating pressure of 3,000 psi.
claims.verbatim: The maximum operating pressure would be 3,000 psi.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 17, rendered image. DNR says Hilcorp later presented this pressure as 'slightly reduced'.

claims.claim: Hilcorp proposed having its facility ready for commercial operation by late 2028.
claims.verbatim: the facility being ready for commercial operation by late 2028
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.suggested_phrasing: Hilcorp proposed commercial operation by late 2028.
claims.notes: Page 17, rendered image, with drilling to start in the second half of 2027. Page 15 says 'by the end of 2028', which is consistent. This is a proposed timeline. The finding gives no ENSTAR in-service date, so do not invent one.

claims.claim: At the September 3rd meeting Hilcorp presented significantly reduced working volumes but never amended its application.
claims.verbatim: Hilcorp presented working volumes under this initial scenario that were significantly reduced, with the maximum operating pressure slightly reduced. The application was not amended to reflect these changes.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 17, rendered image. No revised figure is given.

claims.claim: Cook Inlet's two existing regulated gas storage facilities are permitted for about 38 and 13 billion cubic feet.
claims.verbatim: These facilities are permitted for approximately 38 and 13 Bcf of gas storage capacity, respectively
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 12. The 38 Bcf facility is Kenai Gas Field Sterling Pool 6 (Hilcorp Alaska Gas Storage), and the 13 Bcf facility is CINGSA's Cannery Loop-Sterling C pool, whose parent TriSummit Utilities also owns ENSTAR. Together that is 51 Bcf, against Alaska Public Media's 'around 52 billion cubic feet' (C61). The rounding is consistent. Prefer the primary figures.

claims.claim: The two existing facilities have a combined delivery rate of about 345 million cubic feet per day.
claims.value: about 345 million cubic feet per day
claims.verbatim: have a combined delivery rate of about 345 million cubic feet of gas per day
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 12. Sanity check: ENSTAR's 150 MMscf/D at full build-out would add roughly 43 percent to that (derived).

claims.claim: Annual gas production in the Cook Inlet basin peaked at 196 billion cubic feet in 2006.
claims.verbatim: The AOGCC reports that annual gas production in the Cook Inlet Basin peaked at 196 Bcf in 2006.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 11. Background history. DNR attributes it to AOGCC, so write 'according to AOGCC figures cited by DNR'.

claims.claim: In-state demand for Cook Inlet gas is roughly 70 billion cubic feet a year.
claims.verbatim: gas produced from the Cook Inlet Basin is used for in State demand which today is roughly 70 Bcf
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 11. DNR cites a 2026 UAA ISER report (footnote 4). The page does not say 'a year', but the context is annual. Sanity check: 196 down to about 70 is a decline of roughly 64 percent from the peak (derived).

claims.claim: A DNR forecast projects Cook Inlet production falling below regional demand beginning in the early 2030s.
claims.verbatim: It showed that annual production is projected to fall below regional demand beginning in the early 2030s.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.suggested_phrasing: DNR projects annual production will fall below demand in the early 2030s.
claims.notes: Page 12. This is a PROJECTION from DNR's Cook Inlet Gas Forecast, presented to the Joint Resources Committee on August 20th. Keep 'projected'. It sits awkwardly beside ENSTAR's near-term 18-day winter shortfall warning (C64), which concerns peak deliverability rather than annual supply. Keep the two distinct.

claims.claim: Hilcorp testified on September 10th that it had about 30 billion cubic feet of gas stored in Kenai Pool 6.
claims.verbatim: Hilcorp testified in front of the Joint Resources Committee, that it had approximately 30 Bcf of gas stored in Kenai Pool 6
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 12. This is DNR's account of the testimony. The hearing recording (akleg.gov, footnote 7) was not fetched. Background, September 10th. Pool 6 is permitted for about 38 Bcf (C33), so 30 Bcf is consistent.

claims.claim: Hilcorp said nearly all of that stored gas was committed to ENSTAR for later delivery.
claims.verbatim: nearly all of it was committed to ENSTAR for later delivery
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 12, the same passage as C38.

claims.claim: ENSTAR told legislators the CINGSA storage facility had a significant well sanding incident on January 14th, 2024.
claims.verbatim: on January 14, 2024, the CINGSA facility experienced a significant well sanding incident that temporarily reduced the withdrawal capacity during a period of elevated demand
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 12. BACKGROUND (2024). The source is ENSTAR's testimony to House Energy on February 6th, 2024, as recounted by DNR. Alaska Public Media separately says 'two of CINGSA's wells failed' in 2024 (C62), which is consistent.

claims.claim: The federal government conveyed the oil and gas estate beneath the Kenai Airport to the state by Patent No. 50-86-0386 on August 25th, 1986.
claims.verbatim: On August 25, 1986, the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) conveyed the federal government's oil and gas mineral estate lying beneath the Kenai Airport to the State of Alaska via Patent No. 50-86-0386.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 6, section IV. BACKGROUND. In pypdf the patent number is split across a line ('50-' and '86-0386') and is joined here. This is the root of the state's pore-space claim, which the City of Kenai disputes (C57).

claims.claim: DNR issued oil and gas lease ADL 391094 covering the Kenai Loop field effective October 1st, 2007.
claims.verbatim: effective October 1, 2007, the Department of Natural Resources issued oil and gas lease ADL 391094
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 6. Also on page 1. BACKGROUND. The current lessee is AIX Energy, LLC. The lease went to AIX's predecessors.

claims.claim: Lease ADL 391094 comprises 1,048.640 acres.
claims.verbatim: comprising 1,048.640 acres
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 6. The same sentence locates the lease in 'Sections 13, 32, and 33', but the Attachment 1 map shows it in sections 31 to 33, so '13' looks like a typo for 31. Do not publish the section list (see killed). The acreage itself is unaffected.

claims.claim: The proposed gas storage lease is numbered ADL 394695.
claims.verbatim: the Director has concluded that issuing gas storage lease ADL 394695 will best serve the interests of the state of Alaska
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 20, rendered image. The number also appears on pages 6 to 8 of the pypdf extraction and in the Attachment 1 title.

claims.claim: ENSTAR's application presented an agreement with AIX, the current lessee, to acquire its interest for gas storage.
claims.verbatim: ENSTAR's application presented an agreement with AIX, the lessee of ADL 391094, to acquire its interest in the Kenai Loop Gas Storage Formation
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.suggested_phrasing: ENSTAR has an agreement with AIX to acquire the field, which is subject to conditions and definitive agreements expected in the fourth quarter.
claims.notes: Page 8. Page 1 adds that the acquisition is 'subject to satisfaction of certain conditions and execution of definitive agreements in the fourth quarter of 2026'. Footnote 13 (page 17) says AIX calls it a confidential contractual agreement. Do not say the purchase has closed.

claims.claim: Hilcorp's application included no agreement with AIX, the existing lessee.
claims.verbatim: Hilcorp's application did not include any such agreement with AIX.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 8. Finding 4 on page 19 says only ENSTAR demonstrated the ability to avoid unreasonable interference with the existing lessee.

claims.claim: The Director found the state has clear authority over the pore space tied to its oil and gas estate and may authorize gas storage there.
claims.verbatim: The State has clear authority over the pore space associated with the oil and gas mineral estate and may authorize its use for gas storage.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.suggested_phrasing: DNR asserts the state holds the pore space, and the City of Kenai disputes that.
claims.notes: Page 19, preliminary finding 3, rendered image. It is DISPUTED. Always pair it with the City of Kenai's position (C57). It is a legal assertion, not settled law.

claims.claim: DNR directed ENSTAR to negotiate a comprehensive surface use agreement with the City of Kenai.
claims.verbatim: ENSTAR is directed to negotiate a comprehensive surface use agreement with the City of Kenai consistent with their municipal authorities and obligations
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 8, section VI. DNR calls the City 'the exclusive surface owner' of the airport land and reserves the right to impose extra bonding if no surface-use arrangement is made.

claims.claim: DNR set the original gas in place in the storage formation at 32.5 billion cubic feet.
claims.verbatim: The original gas in place of native gas from the gas storage formation shall be 32.5 Bcf
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 18, section X.C Final Terms, rendered image. Corroborated by Alaska Public Media/KDLL October 16th: 'DNR said the Kenai Loop field used to hold around 32.5 billion cubic feet of gas.' Sanity check: 32.5 minus 3.9 is about 28.6 Bcf produced (derived), which is consistent with 'a high level of resource recovered' (page 8).

claims.claim: Under the proposed terms the lessee would pay a minimum annual fee of $10,000 plus $5,000 for each additional well drilled.
claims.verbatim: The lessee shall pay a minimum annual fee of $10,000 plus $5,000 for each additional well drilled during the term of this lease.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 18, rendered image. These are proposed terms in a preliminary decision. DNR says commercial terms were not weighted in the choice.

claims.claim: The lessee would also pay an annual volume fee of $0.012 per thousand standard cubic feet of non-native gas produced.
claims.verbatim: The lessee shall also pay an annual volume fee of $0.012 per thousand standard cubic feet, computed monthly and paid annually for all volumes of non-native gas produced.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 18, rendered image. Derived scale check: 20.5 Bcf withdrawn would be about $246,000 a year. That figure is NOT printed and should not be published as fact.

claims.claim: The preliminary finding is signed by Haley Paine, Director of the Division of Oil and Gas.
claims.verbatim: Haley Paine Director, Division of Oil and Gas
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 20 signature block, rendered image. Corroborated by Alaska Public Media October 16th, which says Paine, head of the division, wrote the report.

claims.claim: Public comments on the preliminary finding are due by 5 p.m. on November 13th.
claims.verbatim: Comments must be received on or before 5:00 p.m., November 13, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Online Public Notices (DNR Division of Oil and Gas)
claims.notes: Public notice 225521, published 10/13/2026. The finding itself (page 20) says 'received by November 13, 2026' and lists email dog.bif@alaska.gov. Only written commenters can later request reconsideration (AS 38.05.035(i)), which is a useful reader action.

claims.claim: The notice describes about 500 acres of state-owned subsurface storage reservoir in sections 32, 33 and 34 of Township 6 North, Range 11 West.
claims.verbatim: approximately 500 acres of State of Alaska owned subsurface gas storage reservoir
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Online Public Notices (DNR Division of Oil and Gas)
claims.notes: The notice also reads 'Township 6 North, Range 11 West, Seward Meridian' and 'Sections 32, 33, and 34.' Neither ENSTAR nor Hilcorp is named in the notice.

claims.claim: After reviewing comments the Director will make a final determination on the lease to ENSTAR.
claims.verbatim: the Director will make a final determination whether disposal of gas storage lease ADL 394695 to ENSTAR is in the best interest of the state
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas
claims.notes: Page 20, rendered image. No date is given for the final decision.

claims.claim: Kenai City Manager Terry Eubank wrote to DNR Commissioner John Crowther on October 7th about the ownership dispute.
claims.verbatim: In an Oct. 7 letter to DNR Commissioner John Crowther, Kenai city Manager Terry Eubank wrote that the city and DNR are at an impasse on the question of ownership.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media / KDLL
claims.notes: By Ashlyn O'Hara (KDLL). The verbatim is reassembled from two fetched fragments of one sentence, so the join is probable but not character-checked. The letter itself was not fetched, and the outlet is a credible single source. The letter predates the October 13th finding, so it was written while the applications were pending.

claims.claim: The City of Kenai says it owns the reservoir pore space, citing an opinion from Pioneer Law LLC.
claims.verbatim: In its opinion, Pioneer Law LLC argues Kenai owns the pore space
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media / KDLL
claims.notes: The sentence continues 'while the state only owns the gas that used to be in the pore space.' It is the counterweight to C47 and must accompany it.

claims.claim: Eubank wrote there is a very real possibility of conflicting leases that could lead to lengthy and expensive litigation.
claims.verbatim: There is a very real possibility that both will issue conflicting leases
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media / KDLL
claims.notes: The quote is attributed in the article to Eubank's letter. The longer passage reads '(potentially to different applicants) that will result in lengthy and expensive litigation and delay the supply of additional gas to South Central'. The parenthetical and the join were reported in fragments, so quote only the verified string in quotation marks.

claims.claim: Eubank called the omission of disputed ownership from the preliminary recommendation misleading and detrimental.
claims.verbatim: The omission of disputed ownership in the preliminary recommendation is misleading and detrimental
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media / KDLL
claims.notes: This is from a statement to KDLL ('In a statement to KDLL, Eubank said he is "disappointed" the state report doesn't address that conflict.'). Fact check: the finding does contain a Pore Space Ownership section (IV) asserting state ownership, but it does not name the City's competing claim. Eubank's word is 'omission of disputed ownership', so quote it as his view.

claims.claim: The Kenai Loop gas field sits partially under the Kenai airport.
claims.verbatim: sits partially under the Kenai airport
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media / KDLL
claims.notes: Primary corroboration on page 6 of the finding: 'Portions of ADL 391094 lie beneath the surface of the Kenai Airport, owned by the City of Kenai.' The finding places the field east of Kenai Municipal Airport, and the Attachment 1 map shows the proposed storage boundary overlapping the airport. Write 'partly beneath'.

claims.claim: Cook Inlet's two other storage facilities, both in Kenai, have a combined capacity of around 52 billion cubic feet.
claims.verbatim: Both are in Kenai and have a combined storage capacity of around 52 billion cubic feet.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media / KDLL
claims.notes: The primary (C33) gives 38 plus 13, which is 51 Bcf. Prefer C33 and write 'about 51 Bcf' if a single sum is needed.

claims.claim: Two of CINGSA's wells failed in 2024, straining the rest of the facility.
claims.verbatim: In 2024, for example, two of CINGSA's wells failed, straining the rest of the facility.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media / KDLL
claims.notes: BACKGROUND (2024). It is consistent with the primary C40 (well sanding on January 14th, 2024), but the primary does not give a well count. Attribute the 'two wells' to Alaska Public Media.

claims.claim: Southcentral utilities expect natural gas demand to outpace supply.
claims.verbatim: Southcentral utilities prepare for natural gas demand to outpace supply
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media / KDLL
claims.suggested_phrasing: Southcentral utilities are preparing for demand to outpace supply, Alaska Public Media reported.
claims.notes: This is framing context. Optional, so drop it if not needed.

claims.claim: ENSTAR has said it could fall 18 days short of supply this winter depending on temperatures.
claims.verbatim: ENSTAR has said it could fall 18 days short of supply this winter, depending on temperatures.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media / KDLL
claims.suggested_phrasing: ENSTAR has said it could come up as many as 18 days short this winter, depending on temperatures, according to Alaska Public Media.
claims.notes: This is a conditional PROJECTION by ENSTAR, relayed secondhand without a primary ENSTAR document fetched. Keep 'could' and 'depending on temperatures'. Kenai Loop storage would not be online this winter, so do not imply the lease fixes this winter's shortfall.

claims.claim: Division of Oil and Gas director Haley Paine said ENSTAR presented the proposal DNR found to be in the state's best interest.
claims.verbatim: In the totality of all of those, ENSTAR presented the finding that we found to be in the state's best interest
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media / KDLL

killed.claim: An AOGCC hearing on the Kenai Loop storage proposal is tentatively set for November 12th at 10 a.m.
killed.why: Not confirmable on any fetchable page. The AOGCC public notices page returned 403. Alaska Online Public Notices searches for 'Kenai Loop' and 'ENSTAR storage' surfaced only DNR notice 225521, which names no hearing. Neither the DNR finding nor Alaska Public Media mentions an AOGCC hearing date.

killed.claim: The applicants believe the field could store around 17 billion cubic feet of extractable gas.
killed.why: Alaska Public Media attributes it to 'the companies' collectively, and it conflicts with the primary document. DNR gives ENSTAR's working gas as about 20.5 Bcf and Hilcorp's initial claim as 28 to 33 Bcf, so neither applicant's figure is 17 Bcf. Use C23 instead.

killed.claim: That storage equals about a quarter of Southcentral's average annual gas demand.
killed.why: It is derived from the killed 17 Bcf figure. With the primary 20.5 Bcf against roughly 70 Bcf of demand, the share is about 29 percent, which is not printed in any source. If a share is wanted, compute it openly from C23 and C36 and label it as an estimate.

killed.claim: Only CINGSA offers third-party gas storage in Cook Inlet.
killed.why: It contradicts the primary. DNR lists Kenai Gas Field Sterling Pool 6 (Hilcorp Alaska Gas Storage) alongside CINGSA as 'existing regulated gas storage utilities' and says regulated facilities 'provide for third party use of storage space'. This is a disputed characterization, so do not publish it.

killed.claim: Lease ADL 391094 lies within Sections 13, 32 and 33 of T6N R11W.
killed.why: The finding's text says 'Sections 13, 32, and 33', but its own Attachment 1 map places ADL 391094 in sections 31 to 33. It is an apparent typo in the primary, so do not publish the section list. The acreage (C43) stands.

killed.claim: ENSTAR responded to the preliminary finding on October 15th.
killed.why: Alaska Public Media dates Hedlund's statement only as 'Thursday', so the October 15th date is inferred. The quote is kept undated as C66.

killed.claim: Bernadette Wilson is the Republican candidate (party label).
killed.why: Not stated in the fetched KTUU article, and the Beacon piece was not checked for her party. Source it before printing a party label.

killed.claim: Any direct quote from Trump's Wilson endorsement.
killed.why: The KTUU article does not quote the Truth Social posts, and the posts themselves were not fetched.

killed.claim: The Kenai Loop finding involves AI or data centers.
killed.why: Nothing in the finding, the notice or Alaska Public Media links this lease to AI or data centers. ENSTAR's 'dynamic reservoir model' is a reservoir simulation, not AI. Any AI angle must come from bridge claims C71 and C72 and be framed as context (rising Railbelt load interest), not causation.
